text:
ria: Heads-up — new onboarding run exposed a subtle race: our prefetcher starts fetching pages using a cursor that gets rotated by the auth refresh. Result: 401s during prefill, heavy retries, and the client circuit goes soft-open then hard-open.

cheng: Interesting. Is the cursor tied to the access token or is it a separate session cursor?

ria: It's a session cursor from /list endpoint that is valid for the current session token. When the SDK does a token singleflight refresh, some in-flight prefetch requests re-send with the old token and get 401. Then retries align and amplify. Logs: 
```
2026-05-12T09:10:01Z INFO prefill:start pages=4 parallel=4 cursor=cs_Abc123
2026-05-12T09:10:02Z INFO token: refresh scheduled (ttl=8s)
2026-05-12T09:10:02Z WARN http 401 route=/list cursor=cs_Abc123
2026-05-12T09:10:03Z WARN retry attempt=1 route=/list
2026-05-12T09:10:03Z ERROR duplicate page processed id=pg-2
2026-05-12T09:10:04Z ERROR client circuit open: failures=7
```
This was reproducible locally with the python-sampleapp when our IdP returned a short 401 burst during token exchange.

omar: Two different problems colliding: (1) token race + retry alignment, (2) cursor tied to token so retries using old token will always fail. We should implement singleflight for token refresh (so only one refresh happens) and ensure the request pipeline waits for the fresh token before retrying those idempotent prefetches.

lucy: Also the paginator should treat cursor-related 401 as a cursor-expired case and attempt to re-open the list (get a fresh cursor) rather than blind retry. That would avoid duplicate processing and wasted retries.

ria: Agreed. Quick repro steps I used: run sample-python with PREFETCH=4, set TOKEN_REFRESH_BEFORE=10, then run a small script that pauses the IdP for 500ms during refresh.

cheng: SDK parity note: python-sdk currently does no singleflight (every goroutine/request will call refresh on 401 if TTL < window). go-sdk has singleflight logic, node-sdk partially, rust-sdk yes. So parity gap here.

omar: For short-term mitigation we can: 1) change sample default PREFETCH to 2, 2) add a tiny randomized jitter before each prefetch start (5-150ms), 3) detect cursor-401 and mark cursor-stale, then sequentially attempt to reestablish the cursor (one owner).

lucy: For longer-term: 1) add token singleflight to python SDK, 2) make paginator rehydrate cursor on cursor-stale errors and requeue remaining pages idempotently, 3) make prefill honor a "prefill_quiet_period" which slows parallelism while token age < X. Also add unit tests that simulate mid-prefetch token rotation.

ria: Telemetry suggestion: emit "onboard.cursor.stale" with tags {sdk:python,prefetch:4} and "onboard.prefill.rate" so we can correlate first-run failures with token churn.

cheng: UX note: onboarding screen should show a friendly message: "Prefill paused due to temporary auth refresh; retrying shortly (no action required)." New users assume product is broken otherwise.

omar: Implementation plan: I'll open two PRs: SDK change to add singleflight + test, and sampleapp change to conservative defaults + jitter + cursor rehydrate. Lucy, can you do paginator dedupe for idempotency?

lucy: Yep. I'll implement a seen-page set keyed by page-id and make cursor-rehydrate path ensure we don't double-process. Also will add small micro-delay between parallel prefetch starts to reduce alignment.

terraform-bot: Plan updated: sample-python v0.5.3 canary for staging at 2026-05-12T18:00Z.

ria: I'll attach my tiny repro gist to the issue. If someone can review the SDK singleflight patch quickly, that would be great  it should be a small change.

cheng: I'll review the SDK patch. Also will add a lint rule in samples that warns if PREFETCH > 3 in onboarding configs. That should reduce noisy first-run reports.

omar: Thanks team. This one felt subtle because the cursor-token coupling made retries hopeless; singleflight + cursor-rehydrate + dedupe should fix it.

lucy: Agreed. I'll post PR links when ready.

ria: Thanks all — filing the issue now and linking this thread.
